q: Why does a GHG verifier check invoices around the year end?
title: Year-end invoice cut-off in GHG audits
short: Fuel and power used in March can be billed in April. The verifier checks that each bill is counted in the period the energy was used, not the period it was paid. Use meter reading dates and delivery dates, and adjust for bills that straddle the year end.
audience: MSMEs facing a first GHG verification

ul: The last bills of the year and the first of the next.
Electricity bills whose reading period crosses the year end.
Fuel delivered before year end but invoiced after.

p: Split a straddling bill by days or by meter readings. Note the split so the verifier can recompute it.

example.title: Splitting a bill
lines: Bill period 15 March to 14 April: 31 days, 9,300 kWh
Days in March: 17, so 9,300 x 17 / 31 = 5,100 kWh in the year

senseible: Senseible keeps each figure tied to its invoice, factor and method version, so a verifier can trace any number back to the document it came from.

sources.label: ISO 14064-3, verification of greenhouse gas statements (iso.org)
